intent: Archive store backend: OCI registry client (put/get/exists) and trainer upload
OCI archive store client, Docker-config credentials, push command

title: chose a small client on the JDK HttpClient over the ORAS Java SDK
why: Only four registry calls are needed. The core library and init container stay dependency-free, and the one real risk (auth and redirects) is covered by tests against a fake registry and a real registry:2.
alternative: ORAS Java SDK — rejected: transitive dependencies in the fail-open init container, and it still lacks cloud workload-identity token exchange

title: follow registry redirects manually and send Authorization only to the registry host
why: Blob downloads are often redirected to object storage, which must not receive the registry token. HttpClient redirect handling is switched off and 3xx is followed in call().
alternative: Redirect.NORMAL — rejected: header forwarding across hosts is not under our control

title: verify digest and size while streaming, write to a temp file, then atomically move
why: Hundreds of MB must not be buffered, and a failed or tampered download must never leave a usable file behind.
alternative: Download to the final path then verify — rejected: leaves a corrupt file on failure

title: support Basic and Bearer-token auth from a Docker-config file; defer identity tokens and credential helpers
why: A mounted dockerconfigjson Secret is the ADR 0001 delivery path. Cloud workload-identity exchange is a follow-up.
alternative: Credential helpers / identity tokens now — rejected: scope for v0.2.0

name: OciArchiveStore
role: ArchiveStore on an OCI registry: put (blobs then manifest), exists (HEAD), get (verified streaming download)
conditions: Tag is fp-<hex>; downloaded manifest must hash back to the requested fingerprint

name: RegistryCredentials
role: Reads a Docker-config auths entry by registry host

name: push command
role: Uploads build output to --store; exit 2 usage, exit 1 store failure
conditions: Trainer wrapper (#16) decides to exit 0 on failure per ADR 0002

subject: Upload Location handling
why: Location can be relative and may already carry a query, so the digest parameter is appended with ? or &

subject: Redirected blob downloads
why: The registry token must not be forwarded to the redirect target host

intent: Address review: upload location, stall bound, https downgrade, manifest check

title: bound every registry exchange and stream with a timeout; refuse https to http
why: HttpRequest.timeout covers only headers, so a stalled body could hold the init container forever; a downgrade would leak credentials in cleartext. Exchanges use sendAsync with a deadline, streams an idle watchdog, and an https registry never follows an http redirect, location or token realm.
alternative: Rely on HttpRequest.timeout — rejected: does not bound streaming reads

title: put verifies the archive file against its manifest before uploading
why: Otherwise a replaced archive would be published under the original fingerprint, with a layer digest computed from the wrong file.
alternative: Trust the manifest — rejected: allows an inconsistent archive under a valid fingerprint

subject: Relative upload Location
why: Per the OCI spec a Location may be relative or query-only and resolves against the upload-initiation URL, not the registry root

subject: HttpRequest.timeout and streams
why: It ends when headers arrive for ofInputStream; reading the body needs its own idle limit
